Laiba Tahir … Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & Ors. … Respondents 
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Shariq Khurshid, learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
2. Mr. J.C. Pandey, learned Standing Counsel 
for the State/respondent nos.1 to 3.
3. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel 
for Union of India/respondent no.5.
4. Mr. Gaurav Nagpal, Advocate holding brief 
of Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel for 
respondent no.6.
5. The petitioner is claiming admission in 
BUMS Course at Ayurvedic and Unani Tibbia 
College, Karol Bagh, New Delhi against a seat in 
central pool falling in the quota of State of 
Uttarakhand for academic session 2025-26. 
6. The Joint Director, Ayurvedic and Unani 
Services, Uttarakhand, Dehradun by his letter 
dated 16.12.2025, requested the Additional 
Director, Ayush and Ayush Education Anubhag, 
Uttarkhand Department to provide his No 
Objection so that the same could be forwarded to 
the College thereby facilitating participation of 
the petitioner in the counselling process.  7. Learned State Counsel seeks time to 
apprise the Court whether the State Government 
has given No Objection or not and, if not, why, 
and also the present status of the proceedings as 
may have been held in pursuance of the 
communication dated 16.12.2025.
8. Learned counsel for Union of India as well 
as National Commission for Indian System of 
Medicine shall also obtain instructions as to 
whether the seat in question is still vacant or has 
been filled up and also the present status of the 
counselling process.
9. List this case as fresh on 23.04.2026. 
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)

1. Mr. Shariq Khurshid, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. J.C. Pandey, learned Standing Counsel for the 
State of Uttarakhand/ respondent nos.1 to 3.
3. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for the 
Union of India/ respondent no.5.
4. Mr. Ramji Shrivastava, learned counsel along with 
Mr. Gaurav Nagpal, learned counsel for respondent no.6.
5. As per office report dated 28.04.2026 notice sent to
respondent no.4 by speed post has been duly delivered. 
However, none is present on behalf of the said respondent.
6. Shri Ramji Shrivastava, learned counsel appearing on 
behalf of respondent no.6 states that he has received 
instructions from respondent no.4, according to which, the 
timeline for giving admission was 15.05.2025 and it was 
extended by the Ministry of AYUSH by a further period of 
45 days i.e. upto 21.09.2025.
7. By that time, no nomination was received from the 
Government of Uttarakhand in respect of admission of the 
petitioner.
8. The communication about the nomination of the 
petitioner under the State Quota in the Central Pool was 
received in the office of Principal for the first time on 
22.04.2026 much after the expiry of the extended date i.e. 
21.09.2025 and it is for the said reason that the college 
has not given admission to the petitioner.
9. Shri Manoj Kumar, learned counsel appearing on  behalf of respondent no.5 is directed to obtain instructions 
from the said respondent as to whether there could be any 
relaxation in the timeline in the facts of the instant case 
and also bring on record the notification by which timelines 
have been prescribed and the basis therefor.
10. List as fresh on 12.05.2026.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)

orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON’BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON’BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
9TH JUNE, 2026
WRIT PETITION (M/B) No.197 OF 2026
Laiba Tahir --Petitioner
 
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and Others --Respondents
Presence :
Mr. Shariq Khurshid, learned counsel for the petitioner through V.C.
Mr. J.C. Pandey, learned Standing Counsel for the State of 
Uttarakhand/ respondent nos.1 to 3.
Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for the Union of India 
through V.C.
Mr. Ramji Srivastava and Mr. Gaurav Nagpal, learned counsel for 
respondent no.6.
ORDER : (per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta C. J.)
1. The Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India by 
letter dated 08.08.2025 extended the timeline for 
completing the admissions under the Central Nomination 
Quota by further period of 45 days from the date of 
issuance of the letter.
2. In the instant case, the petitioner filed application 
for being given admission under the Central Government 
Nomination Pool on 24.10.2025 i.e. much after the time line
prescribed by letter dated 08.08.2025 had expired.
3. Even the State Government initiated the process 
for inviting applications under the Central Government 
Nomination Pool for the first time on 25.10.2025 by issuing 
advertisement in newspapers. 
1 4. It is also noteworthy that, in case the process of 
nomination is not completed within the timeline prescribed 
by letter dated 08.08.2025, option was given to the donor 
college authorities to admit NEET qualified students under 
intimation to the Ministry.
5. The donor institute i.e. respondent no.4 in its 
communication to the National Commission for Indian 
System of Medicine has taken the stand that the 
nomination for admission under the Central Pool was 
received in the office of Principal for the first time on 
22.04.2026 which was after the expiry of the extended 
period for completing the process of nominations i.e. 
21.09.2025. Therefore, admission was not given to the 
petitioner.
6. There is no material on record to indicate 
whether the timeline prescribed by the Ministry of AYUSH 
for completing the process of nomination under the Central 
Pool was ever extended after the letter dated 08.08.2025.
7. Accordingly, we direct respondent no.6 to clarify 
whether the time line for completing the process of 
nomination under the Central Nomination Pool was ever 
extended after the letter dated 08.08.2025 and whether the 
seat in question was filled up by the donor institute or it 
continued to remain vacant.
8. As it is stated before us that last date for 
admission was extended upto 23.01.2026, on the basis of 
2 the letter of Ministry of AYUSH dated 13.01.2026, 
therefore, we direct respondent no.6 to bring the said letter 
of the Ministry of AYUSH on record so that it could be 
ascertained whether thereunder the time frame for 
completing the process of nomination under the Central 
Pool was also extended or it was only for the purposes of 
filling up the vacant seats on the basis of spot counseling.
9. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the 
Ministry of AYUSH also undertakes to clarify the said 
aspects by filing an affidavit.
10. List on 18.06.2026.
 (MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
 (SUBHASH UPADHYAY, J.)
Dated: 09.06.2026
